question: Tell me about a time when you had a low performing individual on your team. How did you deliver feedback? Did their performance improve?
competency: Hire and Develop the Best (coaching underperformance, feedback delivery)

raiseTranscript.text: On my first project I noticed a teammate missing deadlines on shared tasks. I asked if we could talk after standup and said the delays were blocking the rest of us. I offered to pair on the next ticket so I could see where the friction was.
Performance improved after two weeks. The teammate started finishing tickets on time and we hit the milestone. I checked in weekly after that.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time when you had a low performing individual on your team. How did you deliver feedback? Did their performance improve?
Role: new grad on 4-person project team
Situation: peer missing deadlines, blocking sprint
Action: private conversation + offered to pair
Outcome: tickets on time within 2 weeks, milestone hit
Quote: "I said the delays were blocking the rest of us"
Follow-up: How did you decide what to say? "I kept it to the impact on the team, not personal"
junior.raiseFeedback: Candidate described a clear, scoped example of giving direct feedback to a peer on a small project. The story stayed at the individual-contributor level and showed they owned the conversation and followed up. Performance improved measurably. This meets the bar for junior because it demonstrates willingness to address issues early and track the result rather than avoiding the conversation.

lowerTranscript.text: There was someone on the team who was slow. I mentioned it to my manager and they handled it.
Did you ever speak with the person directly?
Not really, I didn't want to make it awkward.

lowerNotes: Quote: "I didn't want to make it awkward"
Follow-up: What was the impact on the team? "We just worked around it"
junior.lowerFeedback: Candidate avoided delivering feedback themselves and relied on escalation. No evidence of attempting a direct conversation or measuring change. This lowers the bar for junior because the competency requires showing ownership of development conversations even at the individual level.

raiseTranscript.text: I had a mid-level engineer whose code reviews were consistently late, affecting two other teams. I scheduled a 1:1 and shared the specific data: average 4-day turnaround versus the 2-day SLA. We agreed on a weekly check-in and I connected them with a reviewer from another team for calibration.
After six weeks their average dropped to 1.8 days. The other teams stopped escalating and the engineer later became a go-to reviewer.

raiseNotes: Q: same
Role: senior IC owning cross-team feature
Situation: one engineer slowing two dependent teams
Action: data-driven 1:1 + introduced peer calibration
Outcome: turnaround improved from 4 days to 1.8 days
Quote: "I shared the specific data: average 4-day turnaround"
Follow-up: How did you handle resistance? "They pushed back at first so we looked at actual PR timestamps together"
senior.raiseFeedback: Candidate gave a concrete example with measurable impact across teams and used data to make feedback objective. They created a lightweight process (weekly check-ins, peer calibration) and tracked improvement over six weeks. This raises the bar for senior because it shows influence without authority and sustained follow-through rather than a single conversation.

lowerTranscript.text: I had someone whose velocity was low. I gave them feedback in the next 1:1 and told them to pick up the pace.
Not really. They left the team a few months later.

lowerNotes: Action: told them to pick up the pace in 1:1
Quote: "I told them to pick up the pace"
Follow-up: What data or examples did you share? "I didn't pull specific numbers"
senior.lowerFeedback: Candidate delivered vague feedback without data or follow-up structure. No measurable improvement occurred. This lowers the bar for senior because expectations at this level include using concrete examples and creating conditions for improvement rather than one-off statements.

raiseTranscript.text: One of my directs was missing sprint commitments repeatedly. I pulled their last four sprints, showed the gap between committed and delivered points, and asked what support they needed. We created a 30-day plan with smaller stories and daily check-ins for the first two weeks.
They hit 80% of commitments in the next sprint and sustained it. I documented everything in case we needed to move to a PIP.

raiseNotes: Q: same
Role: engineering manager of 8-person team
Situation: direct missing commitments over multiple sprints
Action: data review + 30-day plan with daily check-ins
Outcome: improved to 80% commitment hit rate
Quote: "I pulled their last four sprints and showed the gap"
Follow-up: Did you involve anyone else? "I looped in my manager early for visibility"
manager.raiseFeedback: Candidate used specific performance data, created a structured improvement plan, and documented the process. The direct showed sustained improvement. This raises the bar for manager because it demonstrates systematic coaching, early escalation awareness, and clear ownership of team outcomes.

lowerTranscript.text: I had a low performer. I gave them feedback a few times but nothing really changed so I started managing them out.
What did the feedback sound like?
I told them their work wasn't meeting expectations and to try harder.

lowerNotes: Outcome: moved to manage-out without documented plan
Quote: "I told them their work wasn't meeting expectations"
Follow-up: Did you set measurable goals? "Not really, it was more general"
manager.lowerFeedback: Candidate relied on repeated vague statements without a documented plan or measurable goals. The story ends in manage-out without evidence of genuine development effort. This lowers the bar for manager because the competency requires structured coaching attempts before exit decisions.

raiseTranscript.text: We had a director whose org was consistently missing quarterly goals. I sat down with their skip and the data across three quarters, then had a direct conversation with the director about whether the role still fit. We agreed on a transition plan and I spent time helping them find an individual-contributor path inside the company.
The org's on-time delivery went from 60% to 92% within two quarters after the change. The director stayed and contributed in a different role.

raiseNotes: Q: same
Role: VP leading 200-person org
Situation: director-level underperformance affecting multiple teams
Action: data review with skip + honest role-fit conversation + internal transition support
Outcome: org delivery improved from 60% to 92%
Quote: "I sat down with their skip and the data across three quarters"
Follow-up: How did you balance development versus business needs? "I gave them six weeks to decide on the transition while protecting the team"
exec.raiseFeedback: Candidate handled a senior-level performance issue with clear data, involved the right stakeholders, and created an outcome that preserved both business results and the individual's dignity. The org-level metric improved. This raises the bar for exec because it shows strategic judgment on role fit and long-term talent placement rather than repeated coaching attempts.

lowerTranscript.text: I had a leader who wasn't delivering. After a couple of conversations I replaced them.
I told them the numbers were off and we needed change.

lowerNotes: Action: a couple of conversations then replacement
Quote: "I told them the numbers were off"
Follow-up: Did you explore internal options? "No, it was a clean exit"
exec.lowerFeedback: Candidate moved quickly to replacement without evidence of structured development support or exploration of role fit. No org-level improvement story is tied to the action. This lowers the bar for exec because expectations include thoughtful talent decisions that balance business needs with development and retention options.

diagnostic.junior: Mentions impact on team or sprint
diagnostic.exec: Uses multi-quarter org data for role-fit decisions
Sets transition timeline with stakeholder involvement

diagnostic.senior: Turnaround time improved from 4 to 1.8 days
